published_implementation.note: The first-party repository at the canonical review ref implements the Scientist-to-separate-fresh-Reviewer-to-correction-to-fresh-review architecture described by arXiv:2609.14738. The publication does not expose an exact Git revision for the reported runs, so the result is linked to the system/project lineage but is not relabeled as an execution of the canonical review ref.

observations.benchmark: AppliedScientist iterative reviewer-guided revision study (30 papers)
observations.external_validation_surface: Stanford Reviewer scores saved human-initialized versions independently and is never shown to the Scientist; it is supporting validation rather than part of the measured native review-guided revision path.
observations.comparison_scope_note: The publication compares reviewer-guided revision with fixed-prompt self-revision inside AppliedScientist. Weakness-resolution counts are aggregate closure evidence for the review-guided loop, not a matched cross-harness score.
observations.provenance_limitation: The public repository at the canonical review ref implements the same first-party workflow, but the publication does not bind the reported experimental runs to that exact Git commit. Preserve this as first-party-reported system-lineage evidence, not an independently reproduced run at the pinned revision.
observations.non_claim: This result does not establish a cross-harness ranking, does not prove an exact run revision, and does not determine any canonical VSM autonomy state.
